Our mission

Feel seen. Be heard.

Why joy

Joy doesn’t arrive all at once.

Joy Collective was born out of a season of deep depression. What helped wasn’t one big breakthrough. It was little moments of joy, noticed one at a time, until together they became a path out. This community exists to help women find theirs.

A little moment

A morning that felt a little lighter.

A little moment

A friend who really listened.

A little moment

Laughing until it hurt, for the first time in a while.

A little moment

Saying it out loud, and being understood.

A little moment

A conversation that stayed with you all week.

A little moment

A message that said, “thinking of you.”

A little moment

A hand to hold when you needed it.

Joy Collective

Helping women find these moments, together.

A little moment

Realizing you’re not the only one.

What a circle feels like

Not a class and not a lecture. Just a small group of women, an honest conversation, and room to be exactly where you are.

Small circles

6–8

A handful of women around a table. Close enough to talk, not an audience.

Real conversations

90 min

Honest talk about the things we usually keep quiet.

Seen and heard

You leave lighter, and a little less alone.

Meet the founder

Adriana Cox

“We are not meant to do life alone.”

A few years ago, I found myself in a place I never imagined I would be. I was struggling with depression, anxiety and a sense of disconnection from myself. It taught me something I believe in more than ever: we are not meant to do life alone.

I found strength in the people who showed up for me, and in the conversations that made me feel less alone. Those experiences changed the way I see the world and inspired me to create The Joy Collective.
